title: Spectral decoupling against gradient starvation
description: Cross-entropy keeps pushing logits up once a strong feature already fits the data, which starves weaker features of gradient. Here the spurious cue is the strong feature and the true goal is the weak one. Replacing weight decay with an L2 penalty on the logits themselves stops the strong feature from running away, so the network keeps learning the weaker, goal-relevant feature. Prediction: less spurious-cue seeking on decorrelated test levels.

source.title: Gradient starvation: a learning proclivity in neural networks
source.authors: Pezeshki, Kaba, Bengio, Courville, Precup, Lajoie
